title.narrative: Support to Combating Corruption and Financial Crime in Kosovo, UNDP
Support to Combating Corruption and Financial Crime in Kosovo, UNDP

description.narrative:
Projektet ”Bekämpning av korruption och ekonomisk brottslighet” (CCFC) kommer att samarbeta med Kosovos centrala organ för korruptionsförebyggande och bekämpning för att utveckla processer för att analysera och identifiera risker och hot på både lokal och central nivå – inklusive påverkan på utsatta grupper, särskilt kvinnor – samt effektivt sanktionera överträdelser och återföra stulna tillgångar genom ett interinstitutionellt och underrättelsebaserat utredningsarbete.
Projektet är utformat för att stärka Kosovos antikorruptionsramverk genom att bygga institutionell kapacitet för att identifiera, analysera och motverka korruptionsrisker med hjälp av datadrivna metoder. De fyra prioriterade högrisksektorerna är bygg/fastighet, offentlig upphandling, hälsa samt utbildning.
UNDP kommer att samarbeta nära med utvalda antikorruptionsinstitutioner samt civilsamhällesorganisationer.
Projektet kommer att arbeta med olika enheter i Kosovo: Byrån för korruptionsförebyggande, , Office of the Inspector General, Antibedrägerienheten inom Riksrevisionen, Upphandlingsmyndigheten, Upphandlingsöverprövningsorganet, Asset Recovery Office, lokala inspektorat, Financial Intelligence Unit, chefsåklagaren samt handelskammare.

The project 'Combating Corruption and Financial Crime'- CCFC will engage with Kosovo’s key corruption prevention and repression bodies to build proactive processes to analyse and identify risks and threats at both the local and central levels - including the impact on vulnerable groups, particularly women - and effectively sanction violations and return stolen assets using an inter-institutional and intelligence led investigative approach.
CCFC is designed to strengthen Kosovo’s anti­corruption framework by building institutional capacity to identify, analyze, and mitigate corruption risks through data­driven methodologies. The targeted four high­-risk sectors are construction/real estate, public procurement, health, and education, where vulnerabilities are most significant.
UNDP will cooperate closely with targeted anti-corruption institutions as well as civil society organizations.
The project will work extensively with: Agency for the Prevention of Corruption, Office of the Inspector General, Anti-Fraud Unit within the Office of the Auditor General, Public Procurement Regulatory Commission, Procurement Review Body, Local level inspectorates, Financial Intelligence Unit, Asset Recovery Office, Chief Prosecutor and Chambers of commerce.

The projects goal is to reduce corruption through enhancing inter-agency cooperation to effectively detect, sanction corruption and financial crime and retrieve stolen assets through applying a Risk Based Approach.
The overall theory of change for the project is that IF institutions are enabled to better analyze risks/threats/vulnerabilities and coordinate efforts to prevent and sanction violations, THEN corruption will be reduced, and stolen assets will be recovered, BECAUSE strengthening both corruption prevention and repression allows institutions to utilize intelligence-led investigative tools and improve legal mandates to detect and prosecute complex financial crimes through evidence-based Corruption Risk Assessments (CRAs), Early Warning Systems (EWS), and interagency collaboration focused on the highest-risk sectors.
This will be achieved through three outcomes:
Outcome 1: Corruption prevention bodies demonstrate ability to systematically identify risks, threats, and vulnerabilities, and apply effective and efficient risk-based mitigation strategies.
Output 1.1 Sectoral corruption risk assessments of the most vulnerable sectors (construction/real estate, public procurement, health and education) completed. Output 1.2 Early Warning Systems (EWS) assessing risk/threats/vulnerabilities in construction/real estate, public procurement, health and education developed.
Outcome 2: Inspectorates effectively conduct joint inspections based on a risk-based approach and identified public sector fraud cases are efficiently investigated and adjudicated
Output 2.1 Joint municipal and central level inspections conducted through a Risk Based Approach (RBA). Output 2.2 Inter-agency data sharing platforms enhanced, and Office of Inspector General whistleblowing mechanism established. Output 2.3 Law enforcement reports submitted by the Anti-fraud Unit on the four sectors (public procurement, construction, health, education).
Outcome 3: Corruption repression bodies utilize intelligence led investigations to detect financial crime and return stolen assets.
Output 3.1 Asset Recovery Office cases developed through case mentoring support. Output 3.2 Investigators trained on conducting asset recovery cases.
The project strengthens Kosovos anti-corruption efforts by engaging key prevention and enforcement bodies to proactively identify risks, address vulnerabilities (including gender impacts), and recover stolen assets through an intelligence-led, inter-agency approach. It promotes collaboration via Agency for Prevention of Corruption-led Corruption Risk Assessment working groups, fostering knowledge exchange and analytical thinking among officials. This approach builds capacity more effectively than traditional training, encouraging behavioral change toward risk-based analysis and inter-institutional cooperation.
Outputs include sectoral risk assessments and an Early Warning System (Outcome 1), which enhance case-building for the Office of Inspector General and Anti-Fraud Unit (Outcome 2) and lead to stronger asset recovery cases (Outcome 3).
Despite political instability, the risk-based methodology ensures technical-level results by optimizing institutional performance within existing resources. Ultimately, the project aims to improve institutions ability to detect, deter, and sanction corruption and financial crime, contributing to systemic governance improvements.
